messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple healthcheck failures detected in region us-east-2 for services: route-checker, dns-prober. Alert flood started at ~1759801200. Paging oncall.

alex cheng: on it. can someone confirm if this is real customer impact or noisy probes? paging thresholds look high.

maria gonzalez: seeing rapid error-rate spike from the synthetic probes. sample logs:
```
2025-11-03T14:20:05Z route-checker ERROR target unreachable: dial tcp 10.2.45.12:53: i/o timeout
2025-11-03T14:20:09Z dns-prober WARN response time > 5s for healthcheck endpoint
```
but app metrics (api latency, 500s) look normal for the same nodes.

kyle parker: FYI I rolled out a monitor rule change 40m ago to reduce suppression window. i changed the probe tag filter to prefer `zone:us-east-2b` -> might have inadvertently split targets. investigating.

alex cheng: ok, reduce noise first. jessica, can you mute the pager group for route-checker while we triage? we'll keep one alert channel open for escalations.

jessica reed: will do. applying temporary suppression for alert-route-checker in us-east-2, 30m window. leaving dns-prober noisy alerts to 1/min. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: ACTION: Muted alert-route-checker (us-east-2) for 30 minutes by jessica_reed. Reason: triage in progress. Incident tag: INCIDENT-1759801234.

maria gonzalez: dug into probe backend: probes are targeting an internal LB that recently had a config change — healthcheck path rewritten to /hc -> our probe still hits /healthz for a subset of targets due to a stale service-discovery mapping. that explains false failures from that LB slice.

alex cheng: good catch. can you show the discovery query that returns the stale targets?

maria gonzalez: yeah:
```
# discovery query
SELECT instance_id, health_path FROM probe_targets WHERE region='us-east-2' AND probe='dns-prober' LIMIT 10;
-- returns a mix of /hc and /healthz
```
looks like the metadata tag `health_path` wasn't updated for new instances created by the deploy pipeline.

kyle parker: that matches my change earlier. deploy pipeline now adds a tag `env_zone` and a remote inventory job populates health_path — job probably failed for one AZ during rotate.

alex cheng: mitigation plan:
1) update probe discovery to prefer explicit tag fallback to `/hc` if mixed
2) rotate the inventory job for the affected AZ
3) re-enable muted alerts after validation

jessica reed: applying (1) now — small probe-config patch to treat mixed health_path as `/hc` default. pushing.

maria gonzalez: patch applied, restarting probe workers in us-east-2. logs show retries but succeeding now:
```
2025-11-03T14:35:12Z dns-prober INFO probe ok -> /hc returned 200
2025-11-03T14:35:18Z route-checker INFO restored connectivity to 10.2.45.12
```

ops-bot: NOTICE: probe-worker us-east-2-3 restarted by jessica_reed. health checks returning to OK.

alex cheng: nice. reduce alert suppression to 10m and monitor. if we get sustained OK for 10m, unmute fully.

jessica reed: updated suppression to 10m.

maria gonzalez: running inventory job re-run for AZ `us-east-2b` now. command:
```
infractl inventory refresh --region us-east-2 --az us-east-2b --job-tag health_path
```

kyle parker: also rolling back the monitoring rule tweak that increased granularity — will re-open a separate PR to handle zone splits more gracefully.

alex cheng: customer impact check: metrics show no user-visible error spike. internal synthetic failures only; SLA unaffected. marking impact = none, but higher noise.

jessica reed: unmuting route-checker since 10m window passed and checks stable. ops-bot will resume normal alerting.

ops-bot: ACTION: Unmuted alert-route-checker (us-east-2) by jessica_reed. Incident tag: INCIDENT-1759801234. All systems nominal.

maria gonzalez: inventory job completed: all instances now have health_path=/hc. no leftover mismatches.

kyle parker: opened github issue to add a deployment-time validation step to ensure health_path tag propagation. assigned to infra team. #infra

alex cheng: thanks all. handoff: jessica you're primary for the next 2 hours in case of recurrence, i'll be on standby. leave the ticket with timeline and root cause.

jessica reed: ack, taking it. adding notes to the incident thread and will follow up with a post-incident summary.

incident-bot: NOTE: Incident thread INCIDENT-1759801234 closed for paging. Summary: transient probe-target mismatch in us-east-2 caused false healthcheck alerts. mitigation: probe discovery fallback + inventory re-run. Customer impact: none. Pager noise reduced. Tags: monitoring, probes, us-east-2.

alex cheng: :thumbsup: good job everyone. closing thread."
